engine.principle: Compute market evidence first; narrate only verified results.

question_library.question: When market breadth is this extreme in the current regime, what usually happens over the next week?
Does unusually wide stock dispersion precede a larger market move?
When a recent sector laggard suddenly leads the market, does the rotation persist?
Does the strongest sector trend continue for another week after costs?
After a stock moves this far from its own normal range, does it reverse or continue?
Do stocks experiencing a downside move beyond 2.5σ rebound over the next three sessions?
Do stocks experiencing an upside move beyond 2.5σ reverse over the next three sessions?
After a stock rises at least 2% on twice-normal volume, does the move reverse over the next week?
When volume surges but price barely moves, does a larger move follow?

evidence.comparison_group: All Nifty 500 stock/session observations in range/normal_vol
evidence.outcome_metric: Equal-weight short basket return from next open through session +5

findings.history: Across 8,096 same-regime events, short-side five-session return had a median of +0.57% before the +0.30% cost hurdle.
findings.observation: 10 stocks entered the basket after rising at least 2% on at least 2.0× prior median volume.
findings.question: After a stock rises at least 2% on twice-normal volume, does the move reverse over the next week?
findings.title: A high-volume upside-reversal basket has formed
findings.why_now: Price direction and volume confirmation are both required by the frozen template; basket members are ranked by volume abnormality.

evidence.comparison_group: All other Nifty 500 breadth observations in range/normal_vol
evidence.outcome_metric: Equal-weight market return from next open through session +5

findings.history: In the same range/normal_vol regime, 56 comparable breadth sessions had a median next-week market return of +1.61%.
findings.observation: Fully 75% of the Nifty 500 universe closed higher; this sits in the top 15% of observed breadth.
findings.question: When market breadth is this extreme in the current regime, what usually happens over the next week?
findings.title: Breadth has moved into a historical tail
findings.why_now: Breadth is a market-wide condition, so it belongs at the front of the edition when its evidence clears the usefulness gate.

findings.decision: NO EDGE — HIGH VOLUME DID NOT LEAD TO EXPANSION

evidence.outcome_metric: Absolute stock return from next open through session +5

grading_rule.inconclusive_if: Absolute move lands between the Right and Wrong boundaries.
grading_rule.right_if: Absolute basket move exceeds the frozen 3.41% threshold.
grading_rule.wrong_if: Absolute basket move is below 75% of the frozen 3.41% threshold.

findings.history: Across 215 same-sector quiet-volume events, the median absolute five-session move was +3.21% versus +2.72% normally.
findings.observation: A Diversified constituent traded at 64.4× its prior 20-session median volume while closing +0.12%.
findings.question: When volume surges but price barely moves, does a larger move follow?
findings.title: Heavy volume arrived without a decisive price move
findings.why_now: The template tests movement magnitude only; it will not convert attention into an invented directional call.

findings.decision: WATCHLIST ONLY — HISTORICAL EDGE DID NOT CLEAR COSTS

evidence.comparison_group: All Nifty 500 stock/session observations in range/normal_vol
evidence.outcome_metric: Equal-weight, direction-adjusted basket return from next open through session +3

grading_rule.inconclusive_if: The outcome is inside ±0.30% after costs.
grading_rule.right_if: The rejected trade loses by more than 0.30% after costs.
grading_rule.wrong_if: The rejected trade wins by more than 0.30% after costs.

findings.history: Across 1,522 same-regime stock shocks, the direction-adjusted median three-session return was -0.18% before the +0.30% cost hurdle.
findings.observation: 2 stocks closed beyond the reviewed 2.5σ downside threshold; the basket contains only stocks that independently met the frozen rule.
findings.question: Do stocks experiencing a downside move beyond 2.5σ rebound over the next three sessions?
findings.title: A cross-stock downside-shock basket has formed
findings.why_now: This is a computed cross-stock condition with fixed membership rules, not an analyst-selected list.

findings.decision: NO VIRTUAL DEPLOYMENT — NULL CALIBRATION DID NOT CLEAR THE 10% GATE

evidence.comparison_group: All Chemicals stocks with a same-direction ≥2.5σ shock
evidence.outcome_metric: Direction-adjusted stock return from next open through session +3

grading_rule.inconclusive_if: The outcome is inside ±0.30% after costs.
grading_rule.right_if: The rejected trade loses by more than 0.30% after costs.
grading_rule.wrong_if: The rejected trade wins by more than 0.30% after costs.

findings.history: Across same-sector stocks, 991 comparable upside shocks had a median three-session reversal return of +0.46% before costs.
findings.observation: A Chemicals constituent moved +12.45% today, a +6.3σ event versus its own prior 60-session distribution.
findings.question: After a stock moves this far from its own normal range, does it reverse or continue?
findings.title: A stock move has broken far outside its normal range
findings.why_now: The public card stays at sector level until RA review; the internal evidence preserves the exact stock and comparison set.

findings.decision: NO VIRTUAL DEPLOYMENT — NULL CALIBRATION DID NOT CLEAR THE 10% GATE

evidence.comparison_group: All Nifty 500 stock/session observations in range/normal_vol
evidence.outcome_metric: Equal-weight, direction-adjusted basket return from next open through session +3

grading_rule.inconclusive_if: The outcome is inside ±0.30% after costs.
grading_rule.right_if: The rejected trade loses by more than 0.30% after costs.
grading_rule.wrong_if: The rejected trade wins by more than 0.30% after costs.

findings.history: Across 2,486 same-regime stock shocks, the direction-adjusted median three-session return was +0.34% before the +0.30% cost hurdle.
findings.observation: 10 stocks closed beyond the reviewed 2.5σ upside threshold; the basket contains only stocks that independently met the frozen rule.
findings.question: Do stocks experiencing an upside move beyond 2.5σ reverse over the next three sessions?
findings.title: A cross-stock upside-shock basket has formed
findings.why_now: This is a computed cross-stock condition with fixed membership rules, not an analyst-selected list.

findings.decision: NO TRADE — LEADERSHIP IS ALREADY PRICED

evidence.comparison_group: All sector/session observations in the same regime, benchmarked to equal-weight Nifty 500
evidence.outcome_metric: Sector basket excess return from next open through session +5

grading_rule.inconclusive_if: The outcome is inside ±0.30% after costs.
grading_rule.right_if: The rejected trade loses by more than 0.30% after costs.
grading_rule.wrong_if: The rejected trade wins by more than 0.30% after costs.

findings.history: Prior five-session sector leaders produced a median next-week excess return of -0.17% across 375 same-regime cases.
findings.observation: The sector's equal-weight basket gained +3.28% over the prior five sessions, the best current sector trend.
findings.question: Does the strongest sector trend continue for another week after costs?
findings.title: Information Technology has the strongest one-week sector trend
findings.why_now: Leadership is measured before today's close and compared with every other liquid sector, not selected by narrative.

findings.decision: WATCH — ROTATION DOES NOT CLEAR COSTS

evidence.comparison_group: All liquid sectors in the same market regime, benchmarked to equal-weight Nifty 500
evidence.outcome_metric: Sector basket excess return from next open through session +5

grading_rule.inconclusive_if: The outcome is inside ±0.30% after costs.
grading_rule.right_if: The rejected trade loses by more than 0.30% after costs.
grading_rule.wrong_if: The rejected trade wins by more than 0.30% after costs.

findings.history: Across sectors, 189 comparable flips delivered median five-session excess return of +0.21% versus the equal-weight Nifty 500.
findings.observation: Telecommunication ranked among today's top 2 sectors after sitting in the bottom quartile over the previous month.
findings.question: When a recent sector laggard suddenly leads the market, does the rotation persist?
findings.title: A recent laggard has flipped into sector leadership
findings.why_now: The condition is a rotation, not merely a strong day: recent relative weakness is part of the frozen template.
